key_insight: The paper reformulates FEM PDE solving in an augmented entanglement-basis tensor-network space, enabling efficient optimization with polynomial scaling in the number of elements when bond dimension is bounded.
engineering_relevance: This offers a surrogate-style PDE solver that can handle nonlinear, constrained, and time-dependent finite-element problems without explicitly forming the exponentially large lifted system.
method: Lift FEM governing equations, boundary/initial conditions, and inter-element constraints into a unified quadratic residual minimization in an augmented coefficient space.
Represent the exponentially large tensor-product structure with tensor networks; use MPS as the concrete representation.
Apply DMRG sweeps to optimize element by element and extend to time-dependent problems via implicit temporal discretization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence under both mesh refinement and polynomial refinement on diffusion equations, indicating numerical consistency of the framework.
watch_item: Performance depends on keeping the tensor-network bond dimension bounded; high-entanglement problems may reduce the practical scaling advantage.
paper_title: A Polynomial-Scaling PDE Solver with Entanglement-Basis Tensor Networks
